h1: Central Place Hotel Samut Sakhon — a pool and free parking in Tha Chin for the industrial-estate crowd
intro: If you're working or doing business around the Tha Chin industrial zone and want a hotel with a pool, easy parking and roomy spaces — Central Place Hotel is a 3-star option locals know by name · It sits on Soi 4 off Ekkachai Road in Tha Chin, open since 2005 with 42 rooms · There's an outdoor swimming pool, a restaurant and bar, breakfast service, free parking and EV charging, with rooms from about ฿1,100/night · It's close to the provincial central stadium and roughly 2.5km from Maha Chai train station.

body.html: Central Place Hotel's main draw is that it's a hotel with a pool and free parking in the Tha Chin area, the industrial zone of Samut Sakhon · In a part of town where fully-equipped stays are thin on the ground, this is the name that comes to mind first for people working, attending meetings or dealing with the factories around here · The hotel is on Soi 4 off Ekkachai Road, about 360m from the provincial central stadium, and it's a short drive into the heart of Mahachai.

Open since 2005, the hotel has 42 rooms split between an old wing and a newer wing · Rooms in the new wing are in better shape and more modern, while the old wing is cheaper but shows its age clearly · Choices range from a Superior Double and Deluxe Double to a Deluxe King and a one-bedroom suite for those who want more space · A point many guests like is that rooms are fairly spacious compared with the usual in-town hotel, and the property welcomes pets, which is rare in this area.

What real reviews praise most often is the tasty breakfast, friendly staff and convenient parking · There's an on-site restaurant and bar, an outdoor pool to cool off in, and EV charging that several guests mention warmly since it's still uncommon in hotels around here · For drivers, the free parking and generous space are a real edge over central-town hotels where parking is tight.
"Spacious room, tasty breakfast and good service, plus a pool and easy parking. In an area where it's hard to find a decent hotel, it's good value for a work trip near the estate."

The biggest thing to brace for is inconsistent room condition and upkeep · Some reviews mention getting a run-down old-wing room with weak hot water, ventilation issues and, in a few cases, a smell from the bathroom drain · Cleanliness is where the score takes the biggest hit, so if you book here it's worth asking for a new-wing room and checking the room's condition at check-in.

Another thing to know is that the location isn't convenient for dinner or shopping on foot · The surroundings are industrial and residential, without the lined-up restaurants and malls of the town centre · For a meal out or some mall time, you'll drive into Mahachai or over to CentralPlaza Mahachai, about 6 minutes away · Guests without a car may find getting around here less than smooth.

Overall, Central Place Hotel scores 7.3 out of 10 on Trip.com from around 22 real reviews · It's a sensible fit for anyone working or doing business in the Tha Chin estate area who wants a pool, parking and a roomy stay in the low-four-figure baht range · Rates start around ฿1,100 for a Superior and climb to roughly ฿1,400–1,500 for Deluxe rooms and suites · If you can accept the building's age and uneven upkeep, and you ask for a new-wing room when booking, it remains a solid pick in an area where pool hotels are hard to find.

honestSummary: Central Place Hotel is a sensible fit for anyone working or doing business in the Tha Chin estate area who wants a pool, parking and a roomy stay in the low-four-figure baht range — with breakfast, pet-friendly rooms and EV charging that are rare around here · The trade-offs are a building that shows its age in the old wing, inconsistent cleanliness and upkeep, and a location that needs a car to work well.
honestChecks: If you're worried about room condition — the old and new wings differ a lot, with weak hot water and drain smells in some rooms → ask for a new-wing room when booking and check the bathroom at check-in.

If you don't have your own car — the surroundings are industrial, with little for dinner or shopping nearby → allow time to call a ride into town, or look at a central-Mahachai hotel like The Seaport instead.
If you want a brand-new, spotless hotel — this one has been open since 2005 and shows its age → if newer rooms matter most, look at Phetara Hotel Mahachai or Grand Inter Hotel in this list.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Central Place Hotel Samut Sakhon

faq.q: Where is Central Place Hotel in Samut Sakhon, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Central Place Hotel is at 1242/469 Soi 4, Ekkachai Road, Tha Chin, Mueang Samut Sakhon · It's in the Tha Chin area near the industrial estate, about 360m from the provincial central stadium · It's roughly 2.5km from Maha Chai train station and about a 6-minute drive to CentralPlaza Mahachai.

faq.q: How much does Central Place Hotel cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at about ฿1,100/night for a Superior Double · Options range from a Superior Double and Deluxe Double to a Deluxe King and a one-bedroom suite · Deluxe rooms and suites are in the new wing, with prices rising to around ฿1,400–1,800 depending on season and room type, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Central Place Hotel have a pool and parking?
faq.a: Yes, there's both an outdoor pool and free parking · The parking is generous and there are EV charging points too, which is rare in this area · It's a great fit for drivers and anyone wanting a hotel with a pool in the Tha Chin industrial zone.

faq.q: What are the rooms at Central Place Hotel like — are they clean?
faq.a: Rooms are fairly spacious, split between an old wing and a new wing · New-wing rooms are in better condition, while the old wing shows its age · Some reviews mention weak hot water, ventilation issues and drain smells in certain rooms, so ask for a new-wing room and check the condition at check-in.

faq.q: Who is Central Place Hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits anyone working or doing business in the Tha Chin industrial area who wants a pool, parking and a roomy stay in the low-four-figure baht range · It's pet-friendly and has EV charging · It works better for guests with a car than for those relying on public transport.

faq.q: Is it easy to find food and shopping from Central Place Hotel?
faq.a: The surroundings are industrial and residential, so dinner and shopping aren't very convenient on foot · You'll drive into Mahachai or over to CentralPlaza Mahachai, about 6 minutes away · Without your own car, getting around can feel less smooth, so plan your transport ahead.
